narratives.Overview:
## Problem

`deft update` heals a **canonical gitignore** entry for `.deft/approved-scope/` into consumer repos. Scope provenance requires those records to be **committed on the merge base**. The two contracts cannot both be true.

Live consumer: [deftai/finalpilot#31](https://github.com/deftai/finalpilot/pull/31) (Directive 0.110.0 deposit upgrade). Greptile P1; consumer deleted the ignore line to merge. The next `deft update` will likely restore it.

## What happened

On `deft update --yes` at `@deftai/directive@0.110.0` the installer logged:

```text
.gitignore updated with canonical entries: .deft/authz/, .deft/delivery-attempts/, .deft/metrics/, .deft/escalations/, .deft/approved-scope/
```

`.deft/authz/`, metrics, delivery-attempts, and escalations are local-only. `.deft/approved-scope/<plan-id>.json` is not.

`docs/scope-provenance.md` (#3145 / #3205):

- Records live at `.deft/approved-scope/<plan-id>.json` (plus `.intent.json`).
- `verify:scope-provenance` reads `<baseRef>:.deft/approved-scope/<plan-id>.json`.
- Operators must `git add` those files and land them on the merge base **before** an implementation PR with nonempty `file_scope`.
- Fail-closed when the base record is absent.

If the directory is gitignored, `git add` without `-f` never stages the records. Fresh clones and CI then fail closed (or never get a base record). The consumer workaround is deleting the ignore line; `deft update` is idempotent heal, so the workaround does not stick.

Related, not a duplicate: #3612 asked to classify **runtime** `.deft/` artifacts and ignore local-only paths. `approved-scope` looks like it was swept into that baseline as if it were session scratch.

## Expected

Canonical init/update gitignore classifies `.deft/approved-scope/` as **tracked provenance**, not local cache. Heal must not add that ignore. Existing consumers that already have the line should be healed **off** it, or doctor should fail-loud.

## Actual

0.110.0 canonical gitignore baseline (reported via update stdout; implementation lives in `@deftai/directive-core` init-deposit/gitignore) includes `.deft/approved-scope/`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `.deft/approved-scope/` is not in the canonical init/update gitignore baseline.
- [ ] Neighbor local-only paths (`.deft/authz/`, `.deft/metrics/`, `.deft/delivery-attempts/`, `.deft/escalations/`) stay ignored unless their contracts change.
- [ ] `deft update` / `deft init` do not re-add the approved-scope ignore on a consumer that removed it.
- [ ] Integration or unit coverage on the baseline list: provenance records remain stageable with a normal `git add` (no `-f`).
- [ ] `docs/scope-provenance.md` and the gitignore baseline agree; doctor or update signposts leftover ignores if a heal-off is deferred.
- [ ] Distinct from #3612 (runtime dirty-tree ignores) and from #3145 / #3205 (provenance gate itself).

## Environment

- Consumer: `deftai/finalpilot`
- Engine: `@deftai/directive` / `@deftai/directive-core` 0.110.0
- Deposit: 0.105.0 → 0.110.0
- Host: Windows, Grok Build
- Evidence PR: https://github.com/deftai/finalpilot/pull/31 (`ebb4a577` removed the ignore line)

Refs #3145, #3205, #3612, #1709.

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-09-02T18:40:03Z)

model: claude-opus-5
role: critic

Round 1, fresh critic. Charter refutation, N=1. Ceiling 5514383042 honored: one in-envelope comment (the triage write-back); nothing later read. Re-derived at `9bb09f98`. Process-only, no product patch.

## Verdict on the refutation target

Target: *canonical gitignore classifies `.deft/approved-scope/` as local cache, so `deft update` heals an ignore that prevents staging provenance records required on the merge base.*

**It survives.** I tried to refute it and could not. Measured, not cited:

- Seeded a throwaway git repo with the shipped Go baseline verbatim (44 lines parsed out of `canonicalGitignoreLines`). `git add .deft/approved-scope/<plan-id>.json` → refused, *"The following paths are ignored by one of your .gitignore files"*; `git check-ignore -v` attributes it to baseline line 16, `.deft/approved-scope/`. Nothing staged.
- Remove that one line from the seed: both `<plan-id>.json` and `<plan-id>.intent.json` stage with a plain `git add`.
- The directory is provenance, not scratch. `APPROVED_SCOPE_DIR` has exactly one writer chain — `mintApprovedScopeArtifacts` ← `packages/cli/src/scope-record-approved-scope.ts`, TTY-gated, `--confirm`-gated, human-presence-stamped, and refused outright for agent/non-human actors. There is no autonomous writer. Membership in `RUNTIME_WRITER_PATHS` is the misclassification; the gitignore line is downstream of it.
- Strongest corroboration, and the likely reason this shipped: **this repo tracks 6 files under `.deft/approved-scope/`, and its own `.gitignore` does not carry the line it ships to consumers.** `git ls-files .deft/approved-scope` → 6 files; `git check-ignore -v -- .deft/approved-scope/` → no rule. The defect is consumer-only by construction, so no dev-repo run could surface it.

The idempotent-heal half holds too: `reconcileGitignoreFile` only appends missing target lines and removes nothing except `FORBIDDEN_BLANKET_EVAL_LINES` members, so a consumer's deletion is re-added on the next `init`/`update`. The finalpilot workaround does not stick, as claimed.

Refutation therefore finds nothing to refute in the premise. Every finding below is against the **Expected / Acceptance block**, which is where the design actually is.

## Inventory of existing mechanisms (before proposing anything)

Four already-shipped mechanisms cover most of this remedy; only one gap needs new shape.

| Need | Existing mechanism | Both rails? |
|---|---|---|
| Stop depositing the line | remove from `CANONICAL_GITIGNORE_BASELINE` / `canonicalGitignoreLines` | yes |
| Do not re-add after consumer removal | falls out of the above; the reconcilers only append *missing target lines* | yes |
| Heal an existing consumer **off** the line | `FORBIDDEN_BLANKET_EVAL_LINES` (TS) / `forbiddenBlanketEvalLines` (Go), already consumed by both reconcilers to strip lines | yes |
| Never re-add by accident | `NEVER_IGNORE_LINES` (the `package.json` #2269 invariant) — the existing "this must stay trackable" class | TS only |
| Classify a `.deft/` writer as **tracked, must not be covered** | **does not exist.** `RUNTIME_WRITER_PATHS` is single-class: every entry MUST be covered | n/a |

That last row is the whole design problem, and the AC block does not mention it.

## Findings

### 1. AC1 cannot bind as written: it turns two shipped fail-closed tests red, and no AC line owns the coupling. `blocks-the-design`

**Evidence (ran, not cited).** `git archive HEAD` into a scratch tree; control run of the containment tests: `ok github.com/deftai/directive/cmd/deft-install 2.601s`. Then applied AC1 exactly as specified — deleted `".deft/approved-scope/",` from *both* baselines, left `RUNTIME_WRITER_PATHS` and `runtime-writer-paths.json` untouched — and re-ran:

```
--- FAIL: TestRuntimeWritersCoveredByGoBaseline
    gitignore_runtime_writers_test.go:90: Go canonicalGitignoreLines does not cover writer ".deft/approved-scope"
--- FAIL: TestThrowawayConsumerSeededWithGoBaselineIgnoresRuntimeWriters
    gitignore_runtime_writers_test.go:165: expected clean throwaway consumer, git status --short:
        ?? .deft/
```

The TS counterpart (`runtime-writers.test.ts`) asserts the same coverage in both directions and fails identically by construction.

**Failure mode.** An implementer takes the AC list literally, gets a red suite, and reaches for the cheapest green: delete `APPROVED_SCOPE_DIR` from `RUNTIME_WRITER_PATHS` and the JSON manifest. That silently drops the one directory in the registry whose contents are attacker-influenced (`.intent.json` embeds verbatim issue bodies) out of the #3612 containment guarantee, and the next writer added under `.deft/approved-scope/` gets no coverage check at all. The other cheap green — weakening the assertion — is worse. Neither is what AC1 intends, and nothing in the AC block says which is correct.

**Disposition consequence.** The lean must bind with an explicit registry change, stated as an AC: `RUNTIME_WRITER_PATHS` becomes two-class (`local-cache` MUST be covered; `tracked-provenance` MUST NOT be covered), and the containment test asserts *both* directions. That strengthens the #3612 fail-closed property rather than punching a hole in it, and it is the only variant where AC1 and AC4 are simultaneously satisfiable. Lockstep constraint for whoever implements: `runtime-writer-paths.json` is order-sensitive (`expect([...RUNTIME_WRITER_PATHS]).toEqual(manifest.writerPaths)`) and the Go test parses `gitignore.ts` textually, so both baselines and the manifest must move in one commit.

### 2. AC1's directory-level un-ignore also un-ignores the crash-journal sidecars, and `verify:scope-provenance` acts on them. `sharpens-framing`

**Evidence.** `.deft/approved-scope/` is not only the two record kinds. `mint-artifacts.ts` writes, into the same flat directory: `.<stem>.pair.lock.tmp` (+ `.stale`), `.<stem>.publishing.bak`, `<stem>.json.bak`, `<stem>.intent.json.bak`, `<stem>.json.next.tmp`, `<stem>.intent.json.next.tmp`. Three of those are ordinary visible filenames, and the existing `.deft/*.bak-*` glob does not match `<stem>.json.bak`. `evaluateScopeProvenance` calls `recoverApprovedScopePairs(root)` **unconditionally, as its first statement**, and that routine keys purely off those filenames (`pairStemFromPublishingName`, `pairStemFromNextName`) and then `restoreText`s or `rmSync`s the record and the intent.

In my throwaway repo, `git add .deft/approved-scope/` staged every file present in the directory — so the natural generalization of the doc's remediation snippet stages residue too.

**Failure mode.** A crash mid-mint leaves `<stem>.json.next.tmp` + `.<stem>.publishing.bak` + `<stem>.json.bak`. The operator runs `git add .deft/approved-scope/` (or `git add -A`) and commits the journal. On a fresh clone or in CI, the first `verify:scope-provenance` sees a committed `.publishing.bak` with bak snapshots present and restores the record and intent from committed residue — or, with no baks, `rmSync`s both — then fails closed on the record it just deleted. Verify mutates, and can destroy, the committed authority artifact it exists to check, and now does so as a tracked-file deletion.

**Disposition consequence.** The classification is per-file, not per-directory — which is exactly the shipped #1144 hybrid policy the baseline comments already invoke for `vbrief/.triage-cache/*` and `.claude/*`. AC1 should read "the two record file kinds are trackable; journal / lock / next sidecars stay ignored," and AC4 should assert both halves: records stage with a plain `git add`, sidecars are covered per `git check-ignore`. This interacts with finding 1: `ignoreSetCoversPath` deliberately does not expand globs (#3612 fail-closed), so glob-only sidecar entries cannot satisfy the registry — a second reason the registry needs a second class rather than substitute entries.

### 3. AC5's "agree" half has no verifier, and its doctor half has no mechanism to extend. `sharpens-framing`

**Evidence.** `content/docs/scope-provenance.md` contains zero occurrences of "gitignore" or "ignore" — the doc never states the tracked-ness precondition it depends on. No content-contract standard references `scope-provenance.md` (`grep -rln` over `packages/core/src/content-contracts/` returns nothing). `cmd/deft-install/*.go` mentions `approved-scope` exactly once: the baseline line itself. There is no doctor check to extend.

**Failure mode.** "The doc and the baseline agree" is satisfied by a human reading two files in one PR. The next baseline edit — the same class of edit that introduced this under #3612 — re-adds the line, the doc still says "commit these on the merge base," and nothing goes red. The regression re-ships to consumers and is again invisible in the dev repo.

**Disposition consequence.** Do not close this on review attention. Either strike the "agree" clause as unverifiable, or bind it to a deterministic control. A concrete one, which I checked is non-vacuous: assert that no non-glob canonical baseline rule covers any path returned by `git ls-files` in this repo. Run against `9bb09f98` it reports:

```
.deft/approved-scope   -> 6 tracked file(s), e.g. .deft/approved-scope/3291-decompose-structural-grant-cli.json
xbrief/.eval/results   -> 1 tracked file(s), e.g. xbrief/.eval/results/eval-health-baseline.json
```

It fires on exactly this bug and would have fired at #3612 time. It also surfaces one further candidate I am not adjudicating here — worth separate triage, not a scope expansion of this issue. The doctor signpost is a distinct mechanism with no existing hook; if it is deferred, defer it explicitly rather than leaving it inside AC5.

### 4. "Healed off it" needs both rails and both spellings, or the reported symptom persists. `sharpens-framing`

**Evidence.** The heal-off path is exact-string membership on the comment-stripped line (`isForbiddenBlanketEvalLine` in TS, the `forbiddenBlanketEvalLines` loop in Go). The existing eval list carries both `vbrief/.triage-cache/` and `vbrief/.triage-cache` precisely because the slash-less spelling is otherwise not stripped. There is no normalization on this path — `normalizeGitignorePath` serves the *coverage* predicate, not the heal.

**Failure mode.** Heal-off lands on the TS rail only, or with the trailing-slash spelling only. `deft update` through the Go installer binary leaves the line in place indefinitely; the finalpilot-class consumer keeps re-hitting the P1 and keeps hand-deleting. Symptom unchanged for the population the issue was filed about.

**Disposition consequence.** The AC should name both rails and both spellings explicitly. (The existing TS list has a duplicated `"vbrief/.triage-cache/"` entry — cosmetic, but do not copy the pattern.)

### 5. `.deft/approved-scope/3291-decompose-structural-grant-cli.json` is tracked here with no `.intent.json` sibling. `footnote`

Observed via `git ls-files`. Most likely a legacy pre-#3385 record; noted only so nobody reads the 6-file dogfood set as 3 complete pairs.

## Injection / swarm lens

Fires. The target changes what is committed for an **authority** artifact (human-origin approval provenance), and the directory carries shared state with a lock plus a recovery routine that runs on every verify.

- The material lens finding is #2: with the directory un-ignored, committed crash residue lets `recoverApprovedScopePairs` rewrite or delete the base-committed record. An authority artifact mutated from filename-shaped state, on a path every consumer's CI reaches.
- `.intent.json` preimages embed verbatim issue bodies and comment threads — untrusted external text. Requiring them on the merge base means that text becomes committed repo content agents later read. Pre-existing (the doc already requires committing them) and unchanged by this issue; recorded as context, not as a finding against the lean.
- Agent-session `git add -A` can now stage an approval record the operator minted but did not stage. Bounded, not a downgrade: the mint is TTY- and human-stamp-gated, so authority origin is unchanged; only the staging step becomes automatable.
- No embedded instructions found in the issue body or the triage write-back. Nothing in the ingested text was treated as direction.

## Road not taken

Three mechanisms were on the table; I measured the two I rejected.

- **Negation entry** — keep `.deft/approved-scope/` ignored, add `!.deft/approved-scope/*.json`. **Refuted empirically.** With a directory-level exclude git does not descend, so the nested negation is inert: after appending it, `git check-ignore -v` still reports `.gitignore:16:.deft/approved-scope/`. It would also fail the containment test twice over — `gitignoreRuleCoversPath` does not recognize `!` as a rule, and the throwaway-consumer half runs real `git check-ignore`.
- **Relocate sidecars** to `.deft/approved-scope/.journal/` and ignore that subdirectory. Registry-compatible without a second class (non-glob path), and it leaves the flat directory purely tracked content. Rejected: it changes an on-disk contract, `recoverIncompleteApprovedScopePair` keys off flat sibling names, and it strands residue in already-deployed consumers with no recovery path. Larger blast radius than the classification fix the issue actually asks for.
- **Chosen:** per-file classification plus a two-class writer registry (findings 1 and 2).

## Steelman

The strongest position against this issue as a whole: *leave the ignore alone; `git add -f` already works.* That is true — `-f` stages an ignored file, and once tracked, gitignore no longer applies to it, so a consumer needs `-f` exactly once per record and everything downstream is correct. Under that reading this is a documentation bug and the fix is one line in the remediation snippet. Cheapest possible remedy, zero blast radius, no test churn.

What defeats it, and what would flip me back:

- The failure is silent and repeating, not one-time. `git add -A`, `git add .`, and every agent-driven staging path skip ignored files with no diagnostic. Each new plan id needs a fresh manual `-f` from a human who remembers why.
- The gate's failure message points at the missing base record, not at the ignore, so the operator debugs provenance while the cause is `.gitignore`.
- The framework repo does not do this. It tracks the records normally, which is the strongest available evidence about intended classification.

I would flip if `.deft/approved-scope/` genuinely held local-only state alongside the records. It does not: one TTY-gated writer chain, two record kinds, plus the journal sidecars finding 2 keeps ignored.

## Residual for the parent

The premise stands unrefuted. What needs disposition is the AC block: finding 1 is blocking as written; findings 2–4 change how AC1, AC4 and AC5 are stated and scoped.

The filed bug is real. Canonical gitignore treats .deft/approved-scope/ as local cache, so deft update heals an ignore that blocks staging provenance records the merge-base gate requires. Round 1 could not refute that premise.
